newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan July-Sept GDP data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan July-Sept GDP data.

text.p: Following are a selection of economists and analysts' initial reactions to Japan's July-September GDP (gross domestic product) data. The government said on Tuesday that GDP rose a real 0.1 percent, or an annualised 0.4 percent, in the period from the previous quarter.
"Basically we knew that the third quarter is going to be weak. But it's good that it's actually slightly positive."
"Good news. Capital investment expenditure is continuing to drive Japanese economic growth," Koll told Reuters Financial Television.
He said he expects Japan's GDP in the current fiscal year to the end of March to show a real growth of around three percent.
"The yen's depreciation is going to boost the Japanese economy...Japan's record-low monetary policy is in fact working to pull the Japanese economic cycle towards a sustainable recovery."
Koll added that Japanese economic growth was likely to average between 2.0 and 2.25 percent over the next 15 months.

SOICHI OKUDA, NIPPON CREDIT BANK: "The GDP came in within the expected range. The data is unlikely to change the markets' view that the BOJ will maintain an easy credit policy at least until the end of the current fiscal year in March 1997.

"The data itself is insignificant for financial markets as it is old data. However, positive growth figures are likely to diminish chances of increased public works spending in the upcoming supplementary budget."
RICHARD JERRAM, ING BARING SECURITIES, TOKYO:
"I think there is going to be extreme pressure on the Bank of Japan to compensate for the tight fiscal stance by having a continued super-loose monetary stance."
He said Japan would most likely achieve the official growth target of 2.5 percent in the current fiscal year.
"Next year, I can't see growth getting much above one percent... It (the data) shows that the domestic economy is a long way away from a self-sustaining recovery."
